description: Nine sine LFOs, one for each planet of the solar system and Pluto, each cycling once per that planet's orbit, with a trigger at the end of every orbit and one knob that speeds them all up together

params.text: Speeds every LFO up together, from real time at fully counter-clockwise to an Earth year every millisecond at fully clockwise
Sets every phase back to zero while it is held down, and springs back when released; there is no way to put the phases back where they were

inputs.text: Anything above 0.1V here sets every phase back to zero, and holds them all at zero while it stays high

outputs.text: A 10V pulse each time Mercury finishes an orbit
A 10V pulse each time Venus finishes an orbit
A 10V pulse each time Earth finishes an orbit
A 10V pulse each time Mars finishes an orbit
A 10V pulse each time Jupiter finishes an orbit
A 10V pulse each time Saturn finishes an orbit
A 10V pulse each time Uranus finishes an orbit
A 10V pulse each time Neptune finishes an orbit
A 10V pulse each time Pluto finishes an orbit
A sine swinging 5V either way, one cycle per Mercury orbit of 88 Earth-days
A sine swinging 5V either way, one cycle per Venus orbit of 224.7 Earth-days
A sine swinging 5V either way, one cycle per Earth orbit of 365.2 days
A sine swinging 5V either way, one cycle per Mars orbit of 687 Earth-days
A sine swinging 5V either way, one cycle per Jupiter orbit of 4331 Earth-days
A sine swinging 5V either way, one cycle per Saturn orbit of 10747 Earth-days
A sine swinging 5V either way, one cycle per Uranus orbit of 30589 Earth-days
A sine swinging 5V either way, one cycle per Neptune orbit of 59800 Earth-days
A sine swinging 5V either way, one cycle per Pluto orbit of 90560 Earth-days

notes: no planet is named anywhere on the panel; which jack belongs to which planet is only in the hover text, and the pairs run outward in orbital order from Mercury
the starting phases are worked out when the module is added to the patch, from how far through its orbit each planet would be if all nine had started together at the beginning of 1970
every rate is half of what the knob says: the phases move on every other sample but are stepped as though every sample counted, so at the realtime setting an Earth cycle takes two years
six lamps around the Speed knob light one at a time, where an Earth year is compressed into a year, a day, an hour, a minute, a second and a millisecond; between those settings none is lit
the module is monophonic: every output carries one channel

inputs.0:
high above 0.1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
